details:
Project Details – Space Storytellers

Space Storytellers is an educational website designed to help school-age students and space enthusiasts learn about NASA's abandoned and discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars.

The website presents the stories of important space missions and equipment through separate Moon and Mars sections. Users can explore missions such as Mars Pathfinder, the Mars Exploration Rovers (Spirit and Opportunity), Viking 1 Lander, Apollo 11 Lunar Module Descent Stage, Lunar Roving Vehicle, and Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP). Each story explains the equipment, its mission, and its contribution to space exploration.

The main benefit of this project is that it makes space history easier and more interesting to understand. It helps students discover that even equipment left behind on other worlds has an important story and scientific value.

Our intended impact is to increase curiosity about space exploration, encourage students to learn about NASA missions, and help people understand the history and importance of equipment left on the Moon and Mars.

We developed this project using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. HTML was used to structure the website, CSS to create its visual design and responsive layout, and JavaScript to support website functionality and navigation.

The creative idea behind Space Storytellers is to turn abandoned space equipment into stories rather than simply presenting it as old machinery. The website uses a space-themed design, images, and individual story pages to make learning more engaging.

During development, we considered simplicity, easy navigation, visual appearance, mobile and desktop responsiveness, and making the information understandable for young learners. Our goal was to create an educational experience that connects space history with storytelling.
